arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Castellano argued that repetitive state motions extend the federal habeas deadline.
Mr. Schweitzer argued that repetitive state motions undermine the statutory limitation period.
Chief Justice Rehnquist closed the argument by stating the case was submitted.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the federal habeas statute's tolling provision. The core conflict involves the definition of a properly filed application. One side argues the term excludes repetitive motions. The other side argues the term includes them to harmonize exhaustion rules.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to allow repetitive state motions to extend the federal habeas deadline.
the opposing side wants the Court to reject repetitive state motions as valid tolling events.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that repetitive state motions count as properly filed applications under the statute.
the opposing side argues that repetitive state motions are procedurally barred and cannot toll the deadline.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This issue determines the finality of state criminal convictions. It defines the boundary between state procedural rules and federal habeas rights. It impacts the timing of federal court reviews of state prison sentences.
